title: Hirosaki — 弘前
goal: Read a new place name, understand the clock, and arrange a simple visit.

cards.title: Hirosaki and the Idea of a Visit

blocks.text: 弘前
ひろさき — Hirosaki
Hirosaki is associated with its castle and park, and the park is known for spring cherry blossoms. A short park visit gives us a useful reason to learn **when** something happens.

**弘前に行きます。**
ひろさきに いきます。
I go / will go to Hirosaki.
The city name is new; the destination sentence is familiar. Think back to 富良野に行きます. We will add a clock time to the same pattern, rather than replacing it with a completely different grammar system.

items: **Kanji:** 弘 · **Meaning/readings for orientation:** broad; enlarge; on コウ; ひろ in this name · **Radical and components:** Radical 弓, ゆみ, bow. Modern right 厶 is an abbreviated historical sound element related to 厷 · **Learning role:** Encounter. 弓 is a component clue, not a reason to translate the city as a literal bow.

**Kanji:** 前 · **Meaning/readings for orientation:** front; before; まえ; on ゼン · **Radical and components:** Indexing radical 刀, かたな, appearing as right-side 刂, りっとう. The modern left contains a top shape and a 月-shaped section · **Learning role:** Core. These visible shapes help recognise 前; “moon + knife = front” is not a sound historical explanation.

blocks.text: **弘前 is read ひろさき**, not “こうまえ.” Learn the name as a whole. The さき part is a special place-name reading here; the everyday word “front” remains 前 / まえ.
We can study useful 前 vocabulary without requiring mastery of rare 弘 readings.

cards.title: 前 and 後: Position and Time

blocks.text:
**前** — まえ — front; before.
**後ろ** — うしろ — behind; back.

後 uses **彳**, ぎょうにんべん, as its radical. The modern right side contains smaller shapes including 幺 and 夂. Use these for recognition; the meanings of “thread” and “footstep” do not simply add up to every use of 後.

**店の前に人がいます。**
みせの まえに ひとが います。
There is a person in front of the shop.
Breakdown: 店の前 = the front of the shop; に = where; 人がいます = a person is there.

In clock words, the same characters appear with on readings: **午前 / ごぜん** = a.m.; **午後 / ごご** = p.m. Learn those whole expressions. 午 is an assisted encounter here, not an extra required core character.
**時** — じ in clock times; とき in other contexts meaning “time.”
時 contains **日**, にち/ひ, as its radical and **寺** on the right. 日 gives a time-related connection. 寺 is part of the character's historical sound structure; do not interpret 時 as “sun temple.”

items: **Time:** 一時 · **Reading:** いちじ · **Time:** 七時 · **Reading:** しちじ
**Time:** 二時 · **Reading:** にじ · **Time:** 八時 · **Reading:** はちじ
**Time:** 三時 · **Reading:** さんじ · **Time:** 九時 · **Reading:** くじ
**Time:** 四時 · **Reading:** よじ · **Time:** 十時 · **Reading:** じゅうじ
**Time:** 五時 · **Reading:** ごじ · **Time:** 十一時 · **Reading:** じゅういちじ
**Time:** 六時 · **Reading:** ろくじ · **Time:** 十二時 · **Reading:** じゅうにじ

blocks.text: Watch **四時 = よじ**, **七時 = しちじ**, and **九時 = くじ**. The readings differ from some standalone number preferences and from the months you learned in Asahikawa.
**分** — ふん / ぷん in minutes; a “part” character in other words.

Its radical is **刀**, かたな. The modern upper 八-shaped section and lower 刀 help recognise it; its connection with dividing suggests the idea of a part. **Minute readings are whole forms to learn**, not readings invented from the parts.

items: **Minutes:** 一分 · **Reading:** いっぷん · **Minutes:** 六分 · **Reading:** ろっぷん
**Minutes:** 二分 · **Reading:** にふん · **Minutes:** 七分 · **Reading:** ななふん
**Minutes:** 三分 · **Reading:** さんぷん · **Minutes:** 八分 · **Reading:** はっぷん
**Minutes:** 四分 · **Reading:** よんぷん · **Minutes:** 九分 · **Reading:** きゅうふん
**Minutes:** 五分 · **Reading:** ごふん · **Minutes:** 十分 · **Reading:** じゅっぷん / じっぷん

blocks.text: This course uses じゅっぷん in examples and accepts じっぷん too. Neither 十分 meaning “ten minutes” nor 分 requires knowing all the other meanings/readings today.
**九時五分** — くじ ごふん — 9:05. The hour and minute are read separately.
**半** — はん — half.
半 is indexed under **十**, じゅう. Its upper two strokes and central cross-like form are shape cues, not a claim that it means two plus ten.

**九時半** — くじはん — half past nine, 9:30.
**三時半** — さんじはん — half past three, 3:30.
Half an hour is thirty minutes: **三十分 / さんじゅっぷん** (also さんじっぷん). You can understand 九時半 without reciting a full minute table.
Do not confuse **九月 / くがつ** (September), **九日 / ここのか** (the ninth day), and **九時 / くじ** (nine o'clock). Shared numbers do not guarantee identical readings.

**今、何時ですか。**
いま、なんじですか。
What time is it now?

**九時半です。**
くじはんです。
It is half past nine.
何 becomes **なん** in 何時. 今 / いま means now; you have encountered 今 in 今日, but today's useful standalone word is いま.

**午前九時** — ごぜん くじ — 9 a.m.
**午後三時** — ごご さんじ — 3 p.m.
The number on a clock does not tell you morning or afternoon by itself. These expressions make it clear. We are practising language, not describing the opening hours of a real Hirosaki attraction.

**九時に弘前に行きます。**
くじに ひろさきに いきます。
I go / will go to Hirosaki at nine.
The two に have different jobs: **九時に** = at nine; **弘前に** = to Hirosaki. Identify the word before the particle to understand its role.
Compare:

items: **九時に行きます。** — I go at nine.
**今日、行きます。** — I go today.

blocks.text: 今日 normally does not need に in this simple time use. Do not add に automatically to every time word.

**何時に行きますか。**
なんじに いきますか。
What time will you go?

cards.title: から and まで: Start and End

blocks.text:
**九時から十時まで**
くじから じゅうじまで
From nine until ten.

**九時から十時まで公園にいます。**
くじから じゅうじまで こうえんに います。
I am in the park from nine until ten.
公園 / こうえん = park. Its characters are encounters. います applies to the person staying there; the park itself is a place, not a living subject.

から marks the starting point, and まで the endpoint. They can also be used with places:
**青森から弘前まで** — あおもりから ひろさきまで — from Aomori to Hirosaki.
We saw から in Hokkaido's reading. Now we teach it deliberately and pair it with まで.

**桜** — さくら — cherry blossom/cherry tree, an encounter word.
**花** — はな — flower, an encounter today, formal study later in Hanamaki.

**公園で桜を見ます。**
こうえんで さくらを みます。
I see cherry blossoms in the park.
You know 見ます from Furano. The new park/blossom words receive assistance. This sentence is a possible spring activity in our practice scene; it does not say blossoms are available all year.
If you are looking inside 桜, the 木 on the left is familiar. That links back to 青森's tree family. You can notice a component without adding the whole character to today's mastery goals.

Our fictional note says: **午前九時半に公園に行きます。**
ごぜん くじはんに こうえんに いきます。

items: Is the time 9:00, 9:30, or 3:30?
Is it a.m. or p.m.?
What does the first に mark?
Choose the reading of 四時: よじ / よんじ / しがつ.

blocks.text: **Answers:** 1 9:30. 2 a.m. 3 The action's time. 4 よじ. しがつ is 四月, April.
Now change the note to **午後三時に行きます。** — I go at 3 p.m. Only the time expression changes; the familiar verb pattern remains.

items: **Location:** 弘前 — ひろさき; 弘 is an encounter, 前 is formally studied.
**Position:** 前 = まえ; 後ろ = うしろ; 店の前 = in front of the shop.
**Clock:** 時 = じ; 四時 = よじ; 七時 = しちじ; 九時 = くじ.
**Minutes:** 一分 = いっぷん; 三分 = さんぷん; 五分 = ごふん; 十分 = じゅっぷん/じっぷん.
**Question:** 今、何時ですか。
**Particles:** 九時に; 九時から十時まで.
**Words:** 午前 = ごぜん; 午後 = ごご; 公園 = こうえん.
**Components:** 前/分 connect to 刀; 時 connects to 日; the correct reading remains word-dependent.
**Preview bridge:** 桜 and 花 are assisted; 花 will return in Hanamaki.

blocks.text: **Lesson complete. Next location: Hachinohe / 八戸.**
